frequency_question: What proportion of fully negotiated trade agreements successfully complete final legal scrubbing, translation, formal signing, and ratification within 132 days of the conclusion of substantive text finalization?
membership_rule: Includes comprehensive free trade agreements or economic partnership agreements between major jurisdictions (e.g., EU, US, India, Japan) that reached text finalization; excludes partial scope agreements, investment-only treaties, or security pacts.
provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 7 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 7 major comparable comprehensive agreements examined; all missed the 132-day threshold due to the physical duration of legal scrubbing and multi-language translation.
known_gaps: Excludes minor or single-sector agreements where translation overhead is negligible.
skeleton: Multi-chapter trade agreements requiring legal review, translation into 20+ official languages, institutional review, and signature/ratification steps. Typical minimum sequential calendar duration for legal scrubbing and translation alone is 180 to 360 days, exceeding the 132-day window entirely.
multiplier: 0 hits out of 7 major comprehensive trade agreements completing the post-negotiation legal/translation/signing pipeline within 132 days.
validity_reason: Standard bureaucratic, legal review, and translation protocols for international treaties remain stable over multi-year horizons.
